sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Rock Island, Illinois?
sections.html:
A Rock Island owner can list the house with an agent, sell it privately, or take an offer from a buyer who pays cash and accepts the property as-is. Which one works best depends on repairs, timing and whether the house is owner-occupied or a rental.

Rock Island is one of the Quad Cities, alongside Moline and East Moline in Illinois and Davenport and Bettendorf in Iowa, so the buyer pool crosses the river. A well-kept house can do well on the open market. A house that needs work, has a tenant or sits in a rental-heavy block often does better with a direct sale. Weigh these points before you decide:

  • A listing can reach the widest pool of buyers but usually requires repairs and showings.
  • A private sale saves the agent's commission, but you carry the marketing, paperwork and negotiation.
  • A direct cash sale can close without a lender's appraisal, so the timeline is easier to control.
  • If the property is a rental, the city's rental license and inspection rules may come into play first.

Whichever way you go, ask for the price, closing date and costs in writing before you commit.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Rock Island homes?
sections.html:
Rock Island is a modest-priced market. The Census Bureau puts the median value of owner-occupied homes at $125,900 for 2020 to 2024, and about 35 percent of households rent.

The population was 39,018 in 2010 and has slipped since. A shrinking population with a steady rental market means many sellers are landlords or heirs, and buyers are often local investors. If your house is a rental, price it with the neighborhood's rent levels in mind, since a median gross rent of $842 caps what a buyer can pay and still make a return.

sections.h2: How do the rivers, the Arsenal and the neighborhoods shape a Rock Island sale?
sections.html:
The city sits where the Rock River meets the Mississippi, and Arsenal Island, the original Rock Island, lies in the Mississippi between Rock Island and Davenport. Rock Island Arsenal is the largest government-owned weapons manufacturing arsenal in the United States and employs about 6,000 people, so the base closes a large part of the local job market.

The city's older pockets each have their own character:

  • Downtown and the Broadway Historic District, with well-preserved late 1800s and early 1900s buildings.
  • Watch Hill and the southern part of the city, once the separate community of Searstown and annexed in 1915.
  • The blocks around Augustana College, which was founded in 1860.
  • Streets near the Mississippi riverfront, where Schwiebert Riverfront Park and a casino sit.

Rock Island is also an old rail town. The Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad was founded here in 1851. Bridges cross to Davenport, including the Government Bridge, the Centennial Bridge and the Interstate 280 bridge, and Quad Cities MetroLINK buses use District Station downtown as a hub.

sections.h2: Which employers and schools matter to Rock Island buyers?
sections.html:
The city's 2017 annual financial report lists Rock Island Arsenal with 6,301 employees as the largest employer, followed by Trinity Rock Island with 1,848 and Rock Island-Milan School District 41 with 1,292. County government, Jumer's Casino and Hotel, Augustana College and Modern Woodmen of America each employ several hundred more.

Most of the city lies in Rock Island-Milan School District 41, which runs 13 public schools including Rock Island High School. Parts of the southwest corner are in the Rockridge district. Private options include Jordan Catholic Elementary School and Alleman Catholic High School.

If your address is near a district line, confirm which district serves it before you describe the house to buyers. Many shoppers choose a house by district first and by street second.

sections.h2: What does Rock Island require for rental properties before a sale?
sections.html:
Rock Island requires a city rental license for all residential rental properties, and units must be inspected and meet a minimum code standard before they are offered for rent. Landlords apply through the city's self-service portal, and the Inspection Division sends an email to schedule the inspection after the rental fee is paid.

Inspections are scheduled with the owner or a designated agent, who must be present, and a cancellation fee of $50 applies if the owner does not appear or cancel 24 hours ahead. A Notice of Violation lists items that fail life safety requirements. The first re-inspection is free, and additional compliance inspections cost $50 each. The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time.

A license does not release the owner from fixing violations. If you plan to sell a rental, resolve open violations first or tell the buyer about them, and ask the Inspection Division, at 1528 Third Avenue, what status your license is in before you list.

sections.h2: How is a Rock Island deed recorded and which transfers are exempt from tax?
sections.html:
Deeds for Rock Island parcels are recorded with the Rock Island County Recorder. The office's fee schedule, set by county ordinance effective February 1, 2025, lists $83 for a conforming document with no page count, $64 for certain exempt document types, and $104 for a non-conforming document or one with more than five references. Any document with a legal description also needs the 10-digit PIN.

The state transfer tax statute exempts a list of transfers from the tax, and some of them still require the declaration to be filed. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-45, exempt items include deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100, tax deeds, deeds of partition, deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier deed, deeds to or from government bodies and charities, and deeds issued to a mortgage holder in a foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. A normal sale to a buyer does not fall in these categories.

The recorder also offers a free Property Fraud Alert service that notifies you if a document is recorded in your name. Owners who plan to leave a vacant house for a while may want to sign up before they list.

faqs.q: Does a Rock Island landlord need a rental license to sell the house?
faqs.a: The city requires a license to rent a unit, not to sell it. If the house is rented, though, open inspection violations can complicate a sale, so ask the Inspection Division where your license stands.

faqs.q: What is Rock Island's median home value?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $125,900 as the median value of owner-occupied housing units for 2020 to 2024. Your own house may sit well above or below that figure depending on size, condition and block.

faqs.q: Which county records a Rock Island deed?
faqs.a: Rock Island County. Its Recorder's Office lists conforming documents at $83 and non-conforming documents at $104 under a fee schedule effective February 1, 2025. Confirm the current figure before closing.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Rock Island house?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Rock Island-Milan School District 41. Portions of the southwest part are in the Rockridge district, so check your address with the district.

faqs.q: How many people live in Rock Island?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 36,225 residents on July 1, 2025. The city is the Rock Island County seat and one of the Quad Cities.
